groups.label: Pressure = ___
groups.diagnostic_hint: Pressure = Force ÷ Area (P = F/A). Force is in newtons (N), area in m², giving pressure in N m⁻² (pascals).

groups.label: SI unit of pressure (name)
groups.diagnostic_hint: The SI unit of pressure is the PASCAL (Pa). 1 Pa = 1 N m⁻² = 1 kg m⁻¹ s⁻². Atmospheric pressure is about 101,325 Pa.

groups.label: SI unit of pressure (symbol)
groups.diagnostic_hint: N m⁻² is the equivalent symbol for the pascal. 1 pascal = 1 newton per square metre. The pascal is named after Blaise Pascal.

groups.label: Pressure acts ___ in all directions in a liquid
groups.diagnostic_hint: Pressure in a liquid is EQUAL in all directions at the same depth (Pascal's principle). A liquid at rest transmits pressure uniformly.

groups.label: Liquid pressure increases with ___
groups.diagnostic_hint: Liquid pressure increases with DEPTH. P = ρgh where ρ is density, g is gravitational field strength, h is depth. Greater depth → greater column of liquid above → greater pressure.

groups.label: Upward force on a floating/submerged object is called ___
groups.diagnostic_hint: The upward force exerted by a fluid on a submerged or floating object is called UPTHRUST (or buoyancy force). It arises because fluid pressure increases with depth.

groups.label: An object floats when upthrust equals ___
groups.diagnostic_hint: An object floats when upthrust equals its WEIGHT. If upthrust > weight, it rises; if upthrust < weight, it sinks. At equilibrium (floating): upthrust = weight.
